summary.text: A 52-year-old woman with no known comorbidities walked into the emergency room with decreased vision in her right eye for 1 day after waking and complete loss of vision for 3 hours, after a week of transient right-eye vision loss. She was triaged as Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale category 4, and her arrival vital signs were recorded.

Examination showed perception of light in the right eye and 6/9 in the left, a right relative afferent pupillary defect, a pale macula and multiple retinal arteriolar emboli, and she was diagnosed with central retinal artery occlusion. CT angiography showed complete occlusion of most of the right common, internal and external carotid arteries; the red cell count, hemoglobin and hematocrit were raised and the ECG was normal.

She refused anterior chamber paracentesis and was not willing to undergo thrombolysis, so she was managed with topical intraocular pressure-lowering drops such as Brinzolamide and Timolol, ocular massage and Aspirin 75 mg without significant improvement. Emergency hyperbaric oxygen therapy almost seven hours after symptom onset improved vision from perception of light to hand movements. A thrombotic non-arteritic cause was thought probable and polycythemia vera was considered but not confirmed.

A repeat CT angiogram after two days showed no significant changes. She was discharged on the second day of admission and followed up for HBOT, receiving eight sessions in total. Follow-up visual acuity was 6/18 in the affected eye; the article places the follow-up at 6 months in the case presentation and at three months in the abstract and conclusion.
